land.text: the Magyar tribal union's lands in the Carpathian Basin; Cliopatria's Magyars row (840-910) overlaps this state in 900-910

predecessors.note: Cliopatria draws the Magyars 840-910 and the Principality from 900; the pages opened treat them as one people and one state (the principality was 'established c. 895'). The magyars dossier (another part of eu-15) should end its life at 899 or merge into this one.

land.text: Pannonia, the region west of the Danube, occupied in 900

predecessors.note: Principality page infobox lists it among the predecessors (the table is garbled); Conquest page: Pannonia occupied in 900.

land.text: the eastern area of Great Moravia (Slovakia) occupied from 902

predecessors.note: Invasions page: 'In 902 the Hungarians took the eastern parts of Great Moravia'.

land.text: the Christian Kingdom of Hungary crowned at Esztergom

successors.note: Principality page: 'succeeded by the Christian Kingdom of Hungary with the coronation of St Stephen I at Esztergom on Christmas Day 1000'; the alternative date is 1 January 1001. Transylvania stayed outside until Stephen's campaign against Gyula (see the kingdom-of-hungary dossier).

capitals.name: Árpádváros (Pécs), winter quarters of the prince
capitals.note: No capital is named for the early principality; the page says Árpád's winter quarters were 'possibly in Árpádváros, a district of Pécs', 'clearly after his occupation of Pannonia in 900'. Treat as a seat of the prince, not a documented capital.

capitals.name: Esztergom
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Esztergom and Székesfehérvár (from the reigns of Taksony and Géza)'; Taksony's reign begins c. 955. Esztergom is also where Stephen was crowned in 1000.

capitals.name: Székesfehérvár
capitals.note: Second seat named with Esztergom in the infobox.

rulers.name: Kurszán (kende, joint leader)
rulers.title: kende
rulers.note: Infobox: '890s - c. 904'; Conquest page: Árpád and Kurszán joint leaders in 894; Kurszán killed in 902 or 904 (sources differ). (Reviewer eu-15-b: clipped from 894 to the dossier's start, 900; earlier years belong to the magyars dossier.)

rulers.name: Árpád
rulers.note: Infobox: 'c. 895 - c. 907'. (Reviewer eu-15-b: clipped from c. 895 to the dossier's start, 900.)

rulers.name: Taksony
rulers.note: Infobox: 'c. 955 - c. 972'; styled 'duke of Hungary' in 947 on the page.

correction.text: valid for 900-901 only: the Hungarian plain, Transdanubia west of the Danube (occupied in 900), Slavonia and a quarter of Transylvania; no Slovakia, which is added from 902 (keyframe _902)

keyframe_review.note: 172,858 km2. Conquest page: Hungarians 'attacked and occupied Pannonia (the region to the west of the river) in 900'; before 900 'the lowlands east of the Danube, and Transylvania (Gelou's territory), according to Anonymus' (a late source). Shape checked against the gazetteer: it covers 95% of modern Hungary, 65% of Slavonia, 26% of Transylvania and none of Slovakia or Austria. The pages give no area; the infobox has none. Cliopatria runs this shape to 910, but the same pages say Great Moravia's eastern area fell in 902, so it is cut to 900-901. [orchestrator 2 Nov 2026: from/to set to 900..901 from this entry's own 'valid for 900-901 only'; without them the compiler drew the shape for all its Cliopatria years, overlapping the next keyframe (window p1100-p1199 report)]

correction.text: the 911 shape (Hungary plus Slovakia with Nitra and Burgenland, 232,390 km2) used from 902: 'In 902 the Hungarians took the eastern parts of Great Moravia'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, years only. Invasions page: 902, 'completing the Hungarian Conquest of the Carpathian Basin'; Conquest page: Moravia 'annihilated that state sometime between 902 and 906'; Principality page: Moravia disintegrated and the state firmly established 'by 900'. The pages disagree by a few years; 902 is the date two of them give. Cliopatria dates the same growth to 911.

union.text: Lower Austria east of the Enns

correction.text: the 911 shape plus the lands east of the Enns lost by Bavaria after Pressburg: 'The Hungarian-Bavarian border was then fixed on the Enns river'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Invasions page, July-August 907: 'The Hungarian-Bavarian border was then fixed on the Enns river'; March of Austria page: 'all East Frankish lands beyond the Enns river were lost' in 907. Lower Austria ends on the Enns, so Niederösterreich is the reading (confidence 2). Cliopatria adds Lower Austria only in 922. Styria, which Cliopatria also adds in 922, is not mentioned by any page opened and is left to Cliopatria's date.

union.text: Lower Austria east of the Enns

correction.text: the 911 shape plus Lower Austria, held from 907 on the Enns frontier

keyframe_review.note: 232,391 km2, Slovakia 92% and Burgenland 93% covered. The Slovak growth belongs to 902 (see _902). Lower Austria belongs here too: the Enns frontier was fixed in 907 (Invasions page; March of Austria page).

280,988 km2: the 911 shape plus Lower Austria (94%), Styria (100%) and Vienna. The Lower Austrian part is right for these years (the Enns frontier, 907 to 955; March of Austria page) though Cliopatria dates it 922. Styria is unverified: no page opened mentions it. The Principality page's 'de jure Bavarian-Hungarian border to the River Enns (until 955)' fits the west edge. No infobox area to compare.

261,486 km2: as 922 but Slavonia falls from 67% to 7%. Croatia page: 'Sometime between 923 and 928, Tomislav succeeded in uniting the Croats of Pannonia and Dalmatia', and 'Croatia probably covered most of Dalmatia, Pannonia, and northern and western Bosnia'; the page is silent on any Hungarian-Croatian war and on Hungarian control of Slavonia before 1000. The shape is kept; whether Hungary ever held Slavonia in 900-925 is unverified (confidence 1 in the ledger).

263,706 km2, the same extent as 926 with Lower Austria and Styria still in. March of Austria page: the Enns frontier of 907 stands until the reconquest that Lechfeld (955) began. Unverified beyond that; no page dates anything in 947.

217,711 km2: Lower Austria (3%) and Styria (1%) are gone. March of Austria page: 'Otto I had a new Eastern March (marcha orientalis) erected and by about 960, he appointed Burchard as margrave'; Lechfeld 955 'started the reconquest'. The frontier then ran 'along the Morava (March) and Leitha rivers' with the Gyepű borderland (present-day Burgenland) beyond: the shape keeps Burgenland, which fits. The shape also reaches the Belgrade area (50%) from 960; no page opened explains that, left as drawn.
222,298 km2, almost the shape of 960. Principality page: the intermittent campaigns ended in 970; Géza ruled from c. 972; nothing in the page moves the border. Unverified beyond that.

correction.text: the shape of 990 held to the coronation, 25 December 1000: the principality is succeeded by the Kingdom with 'the coronation of St Stephen I at Esztergom on Christmas Day 1000'

keyframe_review.note: Years only: Cliopatria's shape ends 999 and the Kingdom of Hungary row starts 1000, but the principality lasted to 25 December 1000 (or 1 January 1001). Transylvania beyond the 26% in the shape stayed with Gyula until Stephen's campaign (kingdom-of-hungary dossier).

region.text: the lands east of the Danube, settled by the Hungarians by 900, with the Sava and Transylvanian fringes of Cliopatria's 900 shape

ledger.note: 900: the Magyar tribes hold the Carpathian Basin as a principality under Árpád. Page: the Hungarians 'defeated the First Bulgarian Tsardom and disintegrated the Principality of Moravia, firmly establishing their state there by 900'; infobox 'Established c. 895'; the conquest proper 'started from 894'. The page gives the east-of-the-Danube lowlands only through Anonymus (a late source). The start is set to 900, where Cliopatria's shape begins.

region.text: Pannonia, the region west of the Danube

ledger.note: 900: the Hungarians occupy Pannonia west of the Danube. 'attacked and occupied Pannonia (the region to the west of the river) in 900'; in 896 Arnulf had entrusted Braslav with 'the defense of all Pannonia'. The Principality page's infobox lists the Principality of Lower Pannonia among its predecessors (the table is garbled); the lower-pannonia dossier of another group ends in 900 with the same hand-over. The Conquest page does not say who held Transdanubia in 900.

region.text: the eastern parts of Great Moravia: Slovakia with Nitra and Burgenland as Cliopatria's 911 shape draws it

ledger.note: 902: the Hungarians take the eastern parts of Great Moravia. 'In 902 the Hungarians took the eastern parts of Great Moravia', 'completing the Hungarian Conquest of the Carpathian Basin'. The Conquest page says Moravia was 'annihilated that state sometime between 902 and 906'. The page does not name Slovakia or Nitra; the region is the 911 shape's growth. The Nitra row (898-910) is inside this land.

region.text: the lands east of the Enns, where the border was fixed

ledger.note: July 907: after Pressburg (4-6 July) the Hungarian-Bavarian border is fixed on the Enns. 'The Hungarian-Bavarian border was then fixed on the Enns river'; the March of Austria page: 'all East Frankish lands beyond the Enns river were lost'. The Principality page calls it the 'de jure Bavarian-Hungarian border' to 955. The page names the river, not Lower Austria; the region is the reading.

region.text: Pannonian Croatia, united with Dalmatia under Tomislav between 923 and 928

ledger.note: 926: Croatia takes Slavonia out of Cliopatria's Hungarian shape. Page: 'Sometime between 923 and 928, Tomislav succeeded in uniting the Croats of Pannonia and Dalmatia'; the page is silent on any war with the Hungarians and on Hungarian control of Slavonia before 1000, so this rests on Cliopatria's shapes.
c. 955: the seat moves to Esztergom and Székesfehérvár. Infobox: 'Esztergom and Székesfehérvár (from the reigns of Taksony and Géza)'; Taksony's reign begins c. 955.

region.text: Lower Austria, held on the Enns frontier since 907

ledger.note: 10 August 955: Otto I defeats the Hungarians at the Lechfeld and starts the reconquest of the march. 'In 955, King Otto I of Germany had started the reconquest with his victory at the 955 Battle of Lechfeld.' Lechfeld lies in Bavaria; the page gives no campaign on the Enns, so the contest is the reading of 'reconquest' (the Invasions page dates the battle 10 August).
c. 960: the reconquest ends with a new Eastern March. 'Otto I had a new Eastern March (marcha orientalis) erected and by about 960, he appointed Burchard as margrave.'

region.text: the Eastern March, east of the Enns

ledger.note: c. 960: Lower Austria passes to Otto I's new Eastern March under Burchard (Leopold of Babenberg from 976). Cliopatria's 960 shape drops it. The page dates the margrave 'by about 960'.
960: Cliopatria drops Styria with Lower Austria. March of Austria page does not mention Styria; the date and the counterpart rest on the shape, not on a page.

region.text: the whole principality, succeeded by the Kingdom of Hungary

ledger.note: 25 December 1000: Stephen I is crowned at Esztergom and the principality becomes the Kingdom of Hungary. 'The principality was succeeded by the Christian Kingdom of Hungary with the coronation of St Stephen I at Esztergom on Christmas Day 1000'; the alternative date is 1 January 1001.

wars.name: Hungarian conquest of the Carpathian Basin

zones.text: Pannonia west of the Danube, occupied 900
the eastern parts of Great Moravia, taken 902

wars.outcome: Hungarian victory: Pannonia occupied in 900, the eastern parts of Great Moravia taken from 902, Bavarians crushed at Pressburg (4-6 July 907), which 'is considered the conclusion of the Hungarian Conquest'.
wars.note: The Conquest page (894 against Bulgaria, 900 Pannonia, 20 November 900 Luitpold routs a Hungarian contingent between Passau and Krems, 902-906 Moravia annihilated) dates the stages; this entry rests on the Invasions page for the span and the outcome. (Reviewer eu-15-b: 'from' clipped from 894 to 900, the dossier's start; the 894-899 stages are the magyars dossier's.)

wars.name: Hungarian invasions of Europe
wars.outcome: Raids from 899 to 955 across Italy, Germany, Burgundy, Provence and Spain; checked at the Lechfeld on 10 August 955 ('finally checked their expansion'); the last campaign, with Sviatoslav at Arcadiopolis in 970, 'concluded the Hungarian invasions of Europe'.
wars.note: Only the Enns frontier changed hands; the raids themselves moved no border. The page lists 958 and 961 attacks on the Byzantine Balkans defeated, and in 966 an invasion of the First Bulgarian Empire that forced Peter I to make peace, without territorial result. (Reviewer eu-15-b: 'from' clipped from 899 to 900, the dossier's start.)

wars.name: Reconquest of the Eastern March after the Lechfeld
wars.outcome: Otto I's victory of 955 'started the reconquest'; by about 960 Burchard is margrave of a new Eastern March; Leopold of Babenberg replaces him in 976.
wars.note: The page gives no campaign on the Enns and no month; the five-year span is from 'started the reconquest' in 955 to the margrave 'by about 960'.

wars.name: Koppány's revolt
wars.outcome: The Principality page lists 'Koppány's revolt: 997' in its infobox under Stephen; the page opened gives no further detail, so the outcome is not recorded here.
wars.note: No territorial change is dated; listed so the reviewer sees it was considered.

certainty.note: A steppe-edge principality with a march or borderland (gyepű) on every side; no treaty line. The Enns frontier of 907-955 is the one named line ('de jure', Principality page), but it is only a river and is drawn soft.

notes:
Page budget (5 pages) fully used. The Principality page gives no area, so no infobox comparison was possible; Cliopatria areas are 172,858 to 280,988 km2.

Cliopatria rows: 'Magyars' (840-910) overlaps this state in 900-910 and is, on the pages opened, the same people and polity (predecessor in identity); the magyars dossier should end at 899 or be merged. The Principality's last Cliopatria shape ends 999 and the Kingdom of Hungary row starts 1000, but the principality ended at Christmas 1000 (keyframe _990 extends it, years only).

Not verified by any page opened: Styria in 922-959; Slavonia in 900-925 (Croatia page is silent); the Belgrade area from 960; Transylvania (26% of it in every shape; Gelou and Gyula are Anonymus-era claims). A gap-filler should open 'Gyula (Transylvania)', 'Battle of Pressburg' and 'Carantanian March / March of Styria'.

Counterparts: Principality of Lower Pannonia (infobox predecessor; its dossier exists from another group and ends in 900 with the same hand-over).

Gazetteer: all names used resolve (Niederösterreich, Steiermark, Slavonia, nine Hungarian admin-1 units for Transdanubia). No gazetteer entry exists for 'Pannonia' or 'Transdanubia'; the nine-county union stands in for it.
